turns.t: Morning, doctor. I'm Kerry, I'm Mrs Keane's carer. She's got a lump on her eyelid, and she's been rubbing it.
Good morning, Mrs Keane. Which eye is it?
The right one. The top lid. It's been there a week.
Is it painful?
It's sore, and it's red. And the eye waters.
She's been dabbing it with a hankie. I told her not to. ~
Any change in your vision? ~
No, I can see fine. ~
Anything like this before?
She's had them before. Years ago. And her eyelids get crusty, with that blepharitis.
Do you have any other conditions, Mrs Keane?
Diabetes, just diet, and my heart, a little.
Is there anyone in the family with eye problems?
My sister has glaucoma.
Let me look at the eyelid. Look down for me. ~
Like this?
There's a small, red, tender lump on the edge of the upper lid, with a tiny yellow head at the centre, and the rest of the eye is white and calm.
Is it a stye? ~
Yes, a stye, an infected eyelash gland, I'd say.
How long will it last? ~
Usually a week or two. It often bursts and settles on its own. ~
Do I need drops? ~
Not usually. The best treatment is a warm compress, a clean flannel soaked in warm water, held on the eyelid for ten minutes, three or four times a day.
I'll do that for her. ~
And I'd like you to wash the eyelid edge gently with cooled boiled water, twice a day, to keep it clean.
All right. ~
Don't squeeze it, and avoid eye make-up. ~
I don't wear any. ~
Because of her diabetes, I'd like to check her blood sugar control, so I'd like to arrange an HbA1c blood test.
Can she have it today? ~
Yes, the nurse can take it before you go. ~
Okay. ~
If the swelling spreads to the cheek, the eye becomes very red or painful, or her vision changes, come back immediately.
I will. ~
I'd like to see her in two weeks, to check the stye has gone.
Two weeks. Thank you, doctor. ~

chief_complaint.value: She's got a lump on her eyelid

physical_examination.finding: small, red, tender lump on the edge of the upper lid
physical_examination.normalized_finding: Red tender upper eyelid lesion with yellow head, calm eye

clinical_actions.description: Warm compress ten minutes three or four times a day
Wash lid edge with cooled boiled water twice a day and avoid squeezing or make-up
Return immediately if swelling spreads, eye very red or painful, or vision changes
